## Summary
The region does not appear to encode a typical globular protein. It is best explained as **bacterial upstream/non-coding sequence carrying a tandem direct-repeat array**, with a large open reading frame on the *opposite* strand and a truncated one at the 3' end. The sequence shows no similarity to a standard prokaryotic gene model (no RBS, no −35 chest, no long single ORF on the forward strand). ### 2. antisense ORF — 1177–2213 (345 aa, reverse strand)

- The region ends mid-ORF: the 178-aa protein starting at **fwd 2465..2467 (ATG)** has **no in-frame stop codon** before the end of the sequence (last amino acid is K at 3000; the reading frame continues right off the end of the fragment) — i.e., the ORF is cut off at the region boundary.

- Protein would be 20.3 kDa, mean hydropathy −0.67, net charge +6; no TM helices.

### 4. Possible hairpin in the repeat interior — 493–513
- A 21-nt perfect palindrome: **CGTTGTAATTGATAATGTTG** (stem 7, loop 5) with no mismatches.

## What this looks like
The most parsimonious interpretation: `region_010` is a **contiguous piece of a bacterial chromosome** containing, on the forward strand:
- 1–330: non-coding upstream spacer
- 331–1094: a repeat cluster (13 nearly identical 30-nt copies at 61–62 nt period) — the hallmark of **CRISPR repeat units**, spaced insertion elements, or a phage/plasmid repeat array
- 1095–1176: short non-coding bridge
- 1177–2213: reverse-strand coding sequence (345 aa) — no classic promoter/RBS visible; gene may be co-transcribed from upstream with its terminator further 5′ (outside this fragment)
- 2214–2443: spacer
- 2444–3000: 5' region of another coding sequence whose ATG (2465) and reading frame run **off the end of the fragment**.
